name: Central bank stress
value: Dec Fed rise fully priced; yen near 159.3
summary: Futures fully price a Fed rate rise on 9 Dec; yen near 159.3 per dollar as Tokyo warns against one-sided moves
state: CME FedWatch data put the chance of a rate rise at the 9 Dec Fed meeting at 100%, after Governor Waller opened the door to a half-point move (Motley Fool, 16 Nov). Japan's Finance Minister Katayama warned on 13 Nov of one-sided and rapid moves as the yen briefly passed 160 per dollar, after record intervention in July–August (The Edge Malaysia). The yen was near 159.3 on 17 Nov (Yahoo Finance). No emergency inter-meeting move or new intervention was found.
for_you: Rising policy rates tend to feed through to mortgage and loan costs. Currency swings affect import prices and travel costs.
rubric_hit: Watch: stagflationary dilemma (Fed hikes into slowing growth) and yen intervention threat; no emergency move for Alert

sources.title: There's Now a 100% Chance of a Fed Rate Hike in December
Japan's Katayama warns of one-sided yen moves near 160

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
